scenario.name: Microsoft SQL Server Security & Mandiant DFIR — MSSQL xp_cmdshell / Ole Automation Reconfiguration (EventID 15457) & sqlservr.exe Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a wide multi-lane city highway approaching an overhead exit sign gantry and a row of striped toll plaza booths with automated lifting barrier arms. Cruising down the multi-lane express highway, a driver mounts a cloned electronic toll transponder behind the windshield right before entering the fast-pass lane. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches, then leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the highway toll plaza later. The highway authority’s overhead license-plate camera spots two different vehicles using the same toll pass minutes apart and sounds an immediate toll-plaza alert. In this scenario (T1059.003, Microsoft SQL Server Security & Mandiant DFIR, MSSQL xp_cmdshell / Ole Automation Reconfiguration , EventID 15457 & sqlservr.exe Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sp_configure Reconfiguration of show, then xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load, then cLR Stored Procedure Persistence. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering sp_configure Reconfiguration of show, then xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load, then CLR Stored Procedure Persistence, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell (Application EventID 15457)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059.003 - MSSQL sp_configure Option Reconfiguration)
stages.description: Cruising down the multi-lane express highway, a driver mounts a cloned electronic toll transponder behind the windshield right before entering the fast-pass lane. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the overhead license-plate gantry in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the toll booth attendant go about their routine. Because xp_cmdshell and Ole Automation Procedures are disabled by default (value 0), the attacker executes sp_configure "show advanced options", 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by sp_configure "xp_cmdshell", 1; RECONFIGURE;. SQL Server immediately writes EventID 15457 (Source: MSSQLSERVER) to the Windows Application Event Log and the SQL Server ERRORLOG ("Configuration option 'xp_cmdshell' changed from 0 to 1") (logged in WinEvent Event 15457 with LogChannel=Application , Source: MSSQLSERVER & SQL ERRORLOG, EventID=15457 , Configuration Option Changed, ConfigurationOption=xp_cmdshell , 0 -> 1 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes T-SQL: EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; (which executes privileged T-SQL stored procedures , sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by xp_cmdshell or sp_OACreate 'WScript.Shell' in so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell , Application EventID 15457" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Application EventID 15457 (MSSQLSERVER): Configuration option 'xp_cmdshell' changed from 0 to 1. runs (which executes privileged T-SQL stored procedures , sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE; followed by xp_cmdshell or sp_OACreate 'WScript.Shell' in so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "sp_configure Reconfiguration of show advanced options & xp_cmdshell , Application EventID 15457" under the database daemon's service account). steps.simpleExplanation: When the attacker invokes EXEC master..xp_cmdshell (or sp_OACreate "WScript.Shell"), sqlservr.exe loads C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL16.MSSQLSERVER\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll (or odsole70.dll, Sysmon EventID 7) and spawns cmd.exe /c ... under the SQL Server service account (NT Service\MSSQLSERVER, Sysmon EventID 1) (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate + 7 , ImageLoaded xplog70.dll, ParentImage=sqlservr.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, ServiceAccount=NT SERVICE\MSSQLSERVER , Holds SeImpersonatePrivilege so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 7: Image=sqlservr.exe ImageLoaded=...\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll (or odsole70.dll) (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Sysmon EventID 7: Image=sqlservr.exe ImageLoaded=...\MSSQL\Binn\xplog70.dll so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load & sqlservr.exe Child Shell Execution , Sysmon EventID 1 & 7" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\sqlservr.exe -> Image=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\sqlser so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1059.003 during "xplog70.dll / odsole70.dll Module Load & sqlservr.exe Child Shell Execution , Sysmon EventID 1 & 7" under the database daemon's service account).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 1 (recording EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate + 7 , ImageLoaded xplog70.dll, ParentImage=sqlservr.exe, ChildImage=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe, ServiceAccount=NT SERVICE\MSSQLSERVER , Holds SeImpersonatePrivilege under T1059.003): Run SQL Server under a least-privilege Managed Service Account (gMSA) rather than LocalSystem/Domain Admin, and alert on any child process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned by sqlservr.exe.

steps.plainTitle: CLR Stored Procedure Persistence (sys.assemblies) & Default Trace (.trc) Forensics
steps.storyAnalogy: The vehicle accelerates smoothly through the express toll lane onto the restricted city bypass while every ordinary commuter waits in the cash queue next door. In this final step inside the highway toll plaza, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the highway toll plaza later until the highway toll camera log catches the mismatch.
steps.simpleExplanation: Even if the attacker sets xp_cmdshell back to 0 (generating another EventID 15457 from 1 to 0) and registers a malicious .NET CLR assembly via CREATE ASSEMBLY ... WITH PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, SQL Server’s built-in Default Trace (C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\...\MSSQL\Log\log_*.trc) and sys.assemblies / sys.assembly_files catalog views preserve the exact DDL timestamp, login name, client hostname, and raw PE bytes of the assembly (logged in WinEvent Event 15457 with ForensicArtifact=SQL Server Default Trace , MSSQL\Log\log_*.trc & sys.assembly_files, PersistenceMechanism=User-Defined CLR Assembly , PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, RecoverableBinary=SELECT content FROM sys.assembly_files , Starts with 0x4D5A MZ header so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes T-SQL Forensics: SELECT name, permission_set_desc, create_date FROM sys.assemblies WHERE is_user_defined = 1; (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , T-SQL Forensics: SELECT name, permission_set_desc, create_date FROM sys.assemb so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1505.001 during "CLR Stored Procedure Persistence , sys.assemblies & Default Trace .trc Forensics" under the database daemon's service account). Next, the follow-up artifact Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys.fn_trace_gettable('C:\...\log.trc', DEFAULT); runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , Default Trace Query: SELECT TextData, LoginName, HostName, StartTime FROM sys. so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1505.001 during "CLR Stored Procedure Persistence , sys.assemblies & Default Trace .trc Forensics" under the database daemon's service account).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in WinEvent Event 15457 (recording ForensicArtifact=SQL Server Default Trace , MSSQL\Log\log_*.trc & sys.assembly_files, PersistenceMechanism=User-Defined CLR Assembly , PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, RecoverableBinary=SELECT content FROM sys.assembly_files , Starts with 0x4D5A MZ header under T1505.001): Query sys.assemblies and sys.fn_trace_gettable on the SQL Server Default Trace (.trc) during database DFIR investigations to recover schema/configuration changes and extract malicious CLR assemblies.
